chunks: And with the preceding chain, from 'Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the 'shiqraq' (2), so he said:

"Its killing is disliked due to the presence of snakes." He said, "And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was walking one day when a 'shiqraq' had broken [its back], so he extracted a snake from his two shoes."

key_terms.الشِّقِرَّاق: A type of lizard or small reptile
key_terms.لِحَالِ الْحَيَّاتِ: Due to the presence of snakes

ai.seo_question: Why is killing the shiqraq disliked in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that killing the 'shiqraq' is disliked (makruh) due to its symbiotic relationship with snakes, a concept rooted in the natural observation that they often coexist. This ruling is substantiated by a prophetic narrative where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) extracted a snake from his shoe after encountering a broken shiqraq, illustrating the tangible link between the two creatures in the physical world. This hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on deriving legal rulings from observable natural phenomena and the wisdom embedded in prophetic experiences.
